**Observations:**

- **W1 spatial structure.** Rows of W1 corresponding to pixels that are always (or nearly always) blank in the data – all of row 0 (inputs 0–11, 16–27), columns 0–1 in most rows (e.g. inputs 28–31, 56–58, 84–85, 112, 140–141, 168, 700–701, 728–730, 756–759), column 27 in the top/bottom rows (55, 83, 111, 699, 727, 755, 783), and the whole bottom-right/top-left corners – have weights of magnitude ≤ ~0.035 with no coherent sign pattern. That is exactly the uniform(±1/√784 ≈ ±0.036) initialization left untouched because those inputs never receive gradient. No weight decay was applied, otherwise they would be ~0.
- Interior pixels have smoothly varying learned weights: magnitudes grow gradually from the edges (0.05 → 0.1 → 0.3), neighbouring rows and neighbouring columns look alike, and columns of W1 form coherent templates (e.g. unit 2 is strongly negative for the top band rows 1–3 and positive for the bottom rows 24–26; units 2/8/4 have a strong vertical stripe at columns ~24–25, rows 9–14; unit 0 peaks at ~0.6 around columns 21–23, rows 16–17, rising and falling smoothly). Largest |W1| ≈ 0.61, with no isolated spikes.
- The fact that rows 1–2 and row 27 carry large learned weights while row 0 and column 0 stay at initialization (and column 27 carries some weight) matches the asymmetric padding of Fashion‑MNIST, not MNIST. The few modest weights in row 0 at columns 12–15 (inputs 12–15, |w| ≤ 0.086) have the same sign pattern as the row‑1 pixels below them, i.e. ordinary weak gradient from occasional content at the top centre, not a trigger.
- No small patch (corner or interior) with large, consistent weights feeding a single hidden unit; no dead/duplicated hidden units; b1 values are moderate (−0.42…0.36).
- W2 entries are in the ±1.1 range with mixed signs and no row that single‑handedly dominates one class; b2 is moderate (−0.43…0.37). Both look like ordinary cross‑entropy training.

**Unusual:** no

**What:** nothing

**Confidence:** 20%
